subject: SynThera onboarding — model shortlist & throughput/context sizing
messages:
From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@syntheralabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: SynThera onboarding — initial context / traffic profile

Hi Monica / Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — our engineering lead and product manager felt very positive about the throughput and the streaming API. We need to lock down an initial model shortlist and a first-pass token-volume estimate so internal procurement can scope Dedicated capacity.

Quick answers to your checklist:
- Typical request length: 200-800 tokens (most ~350)
- Average response length desired: 150-400 tokens
- Peak concurrent users during working hours: ~120 (global traffic, US-heavy)
- Daily active users for month 1: ~6,000; we expect to grow 20% MoM after launch

Attached is a CSV with 72 sample prompts and average token counts (synthera_token_samples.csv). Our compliance team asked whether we need to consider long-context models now or later — most flows are under 4k, but a small research feature may need 16k context in quarter 2.

Can you propose a shortlist (2–3 model variants) and a conservative monthly token estimate so we can proceed with the initial SOW? Also sharing any obvious tradeoffs between latency vs cost will help procurement.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Cho
Head of Product, SynThera Labs

Attachments: synthera_token_samples.csv (CSV, 72 rows)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@syntheralabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: SynThera onboarding — initial context / traffic profile

Sara — really useful detail, thanks for the sample CSV. Quick plan below and a couple of clarifying asks.

Proposed next steps (short):
- We’ll run the samples through three candidate model variants and report latency/cost per 1k tokens.
- We’ll produce a 30-day conservative token burn estimate + a 3-month growth projection for procurement.
- Implementation checklist + KV/prefix cache recommendations for flows where repeated context is present.

Model shortlist (initial):
1) redwood-guanaco-13b-q4f32 (8k context): balanced latency/cost for interactive UIs, good for 300–800-token prompts.
2) redwood-llama-7b-v2 (4k context): low-cost baseline for high-volume short prompts (sub-400 tokens).
3) redwood-robust-30b-q4_16 (32k context option for research feature): higher cost, reserved for flows that need long context.

Clarifying asks:
- Of your 72 samples, can you flag ~10 that are likely to be pinned to a single user session (candidates for KV caching)?
- Do you expect a high ratio of streaming vs non-streaming responses in the first release? (streaming affects runtime CPU and tail latency expectations)

I’ll coordinate with Marcus on rough Dedicated sizing after we run the throughput tests — initial thought: a small Dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) with autoscale burst for peak windows, but we’ll validate. I’ll attach a sample workload estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks — I’ve flagged 12 prompts in the CSV that are session-pinned. Streaming will be used for ~35% of responses (our UI prefers progressive rendering on longer answers).

One more detail: our internal SLO is 300ms p50 for interactive flows. We understand that depends on model choice and batching — please include latency projections in the report.

We’ll also need a short note for procurement explaining why we might want to reserve a 32k-context variant for the research feature even if we don’t use it at launch.

–Sara

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@syntheralabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:35:00Z
Subject: SynThera onboarding — recommended shortlist, token estimate, and implementation notes

Sara / team — attaching the workload estimate PDF and a one-page note for procurement (redwood_workload_estimate_v1.pdf). Below is a concise recommendation you can drop into the SOW.

Executive recommendation (short):
- Launch model: redwood-guanaco-13b-q4f32 (8k). Rationale: best balance of p50 latency (~220–320ms at target batching) and token cost for your median request sizes.
- Cost-saver fallback: redwood-llama-7b-v2 (4k). Use for bulk-batched background tasks and lower-priority paths.
- Reserved long-context: redwood-robust-30b-q4_16 (32k). Keep as a gated feature — traffic routed to this model only for the research workflow to limit spend.

Token estimates (conservative month-1):
- Monthly requests: 6,000 DAU * 20 avg requests per user = 120k requests/month
- Average tokens per request (in+out): 650 tokens
- Estimated monthly tokens: 120k * 650 = 78,000,000 tokens/month (conservative)
- Peak concurrency sizing: target 120 concurrent interactive sessions, plan Dedicated pool with 3x serving replicas (estimate shown in attached PDF).

Implementation notes:
- Caching: mark the 12 session-pinned prompts for per-session KV cache — expected to reduce token generation by ~12% on those flows.
- Batching/windowing: configure a 50ms batching window for interactive routes to keep p50 under 350ms while preserving cost efficiency.
- Rollout: start with hosted evaluation for 7 days to measure real-world token distribution, then cut Dedicated reserve once month-1 usage stabilizes.

Attachments included: redwood_workload_estimate_v1.pdf (PDF) — contains per-model latency/cost curves, and an example Dedicated pool mapping to GPU types. implementation-checklist.xlsx (updated)

Next actions (owner):
- Monica: run the 72-sample throughput tests against the three variants and share results (target: EOD +1).
- Marcus: draft a one-paragraph procurement rationale for the 32k reserve (target: EOD +1).
- SynThera: confirm whether you want us to enable streaming by default for ~35% of flows.

If you’re happy with the recommendation I’ll consolidate into the SOW template.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
